brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Vertical stack at 0,0,0 / 0,0,1 / 0,0,2 (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:0,0,1;full, piece:0,0,2;full with snap connectors)
Two notch drawer frames on level 0: notch:0#0,1#notch1 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) and notch:0#1,-1#notch4 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) positioned between touching full bases 0,0,0 and 1,0,0

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,2~hex-bin-full (hex-bin-full) placed inside piece:0,0,2;full at level 2

finish.summary: Built a 3-storey column at 0,0,0-2. Bottom storey (level 0) has two adjacent full bases enabling two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm / mf) as drawers. Top storey (level 2) has an open hex-bin-full bin. Mesh clash clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
